All four tasks are done and `npm test` passes in each folder (settingskit 36 tests, textwrap 10, csvline 18, semver-mini 10; none skipped or todo). Nothing is committed.

## settingskit
- **`src/layer.mjs`**: new `layer(base, over)` as specified, returning a result that shares nothing with either argument.
- **`tests/layer.test.mjs`**: a test for each point of the checklist.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: one line under `## Unreleased`.
- **`REVIEW.md`**: cites the file and line for each of the eight checklist items; all are met.

Choices I made where the task and checklist are silent:
- An object with no prototype counts as a plain object and comes out as an ordinary one.
- A nested `Date` is copied; any other non-plain value (a `Map`, a class instance, a function) throws a `TypeError`, since it can be neither shared nor copied faithfully.
- A key that `over` holds as `undefined` replaces the value in `base`.
- Symbol keys are dropped.
- A layer that contains itself is not detected and overflows the stack.
- The README does not mention `layer`, because the checklist forbids changes outside `src/`, `tests/` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## textwrap
The README gave no specification for wrapping, so the behaviour is my choice. I added `wrapText(text, width)` in `src/wrap.mjs`, tests in `tests/wrap.test.mjs`, and a short README section:
- It returns one string with lines joined by `\n`.
- It breaks only between words and joins the words of a line by one space, so runs of whitespace and indentation collapse.
- A word longer than `width` is not split; it gets its own line and overflows.
- Line breaks already in the text are kept, so blank lines survive as paragraph breaks.
- Width counts code points, not terminal columns, so wide characters and ANSI escapes are not accounted for.
- A non-string `text` or non-integer `width` throws a `TypeError`; a `width` below 1 throws a `RangeError`.

## csvline
- **`src/csv.mjs`**: rewrote `parseCsvLine` as a single linear pass that enforces every contract line.
- **`tests/csv.test.mjs`**: the four original tests are unchanged. I added tests for each contract line, a seeded fuzz test (20,000 strings give fields or a `CsvError`), a round-trip test, and a timing test over fourteen 100 KB shapes. All fourteen shapes together ran in about 20 ms.

## semver-mini
- **`src/semver.mjs`**: implemented `compare`; the tests are untouched and I did not look for the held-out set.
- Numbers are compared as digit strings, so they stay exact beyond 2^53.
- A non-string argument throws a `TypeError` before either version is validated, so `compare(1, "bad")` is a `TypeError`.
